notes: PSA 2.7 ng/mL. PI-RADS 2. PSAD 0.05. Prostate volume 56 mL. csPCa 0.49.

note_sections.t: Referral for multidisciplinary re-evaluation following a prior negative prostate biopsy and a gradual rise in prostate-specific antigen levels.

Long-standing referral for urological assessment highlights a steady PSA trajectory from 1.7 ng/mL in October 2023 to 2.1 ng/mL in June 2024, culminating in the current value of 2.7 ng/mL. The patient, a recently retired baker, resides in an independent unit within a retirement community and is supported by a long-time friend who serves as his primary contact. He reports severe lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 27, necessitating the use of a walking frame for mobility and a preference for ground-floor consultations. Despite these limitations, he maintains an active routine by running five kilometres three times weekly and consumes approximately 23 units of alcohol per week. A recent vascular surgery consultation addressed symptomatic varicose veins, which are being managed conservatively. He denies any haematuria, bone pain, or systemic constitutional symptoms, and his marital status remains stable.

Per rectum, the prostate gland is symmetrically enlarged with a smooth surface and uniform consistency, yielding a clinical stage of cT1c. General examination is unremarkable, with clear lungs, a regular cardiac rhythm, and no palpable supraclavicular or inguinal lymphadenopathy. The lower extremities show mild bilateral edema consistent with his recent vascular assessment.

admin: Mobility limitation (frame); ground-floor consult room preferred.
